The tool used for writing is a pen (or pencil, stylus, keyboard, etc., depending on the medium, but traditionally a pen).

In the provided text, several symbols and metaphors convey themes of isolation, freedom, and existential reflection. The "vast, open sea" serves as a metaphor for the infinite unknown or the boundless nature of existence. By describing the ocean as "indifferent and ageless," the author personifies the sea to highlight human insignificance against the backdrop of eternity. The "small boat" represents Miranda’s fragile, solitary existence or consciousness, emphasized by the phrase "only speck of reality," which suggests that her presence is the only tangible anchor in an abstract, overwhelming world. The sea’s whisper of "freedom and escape" acts as a metaphor for the seductive allure of letting go of earthly constraints, while the act of floating symbolizes surrender to the flow of life or fate.
